title: the cost a user sees is the cost they paid
description: Tasks: (1) Price table rows for claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5 at its current price and claude-fable-5-1 (cache read 0.25), with pricingAsOf and the source URL; the hook-side copy stays equal through pricing_divergences. (2) Print attribution coverage beside every cost-per-task figure (tasks with any attributed tokens / tasks done; main loop not attributed). (3) Pilot reading Claude Code's own costUSD or OTel cost instead of the plugin's table, and retire the table if it holds.
desiredOutcome: every cost the plugin prints uses current official prices with their date and source, and every per-task cost says how much of the work it actually attributes

findings.issue: The phase outcome says every cost is printed with its date and source, but no surface prints the source: PRICING_SOURCE_URL and pricing_provenance_divergences() are read only by tests, and the report, its Markdown twin, /audit:usage, the panel and /audit:status print only 'rates as of <date>' or 'rates undated'.
findings.resolution: fixed in P104.11-tog (308189d6): Extend the one rate-basis phrase each surface prints so it names the source beside the date (the shipped table's source URL, or the project's own usage.pricing), built in one Python helper the report, twin, CLI and status call, served to the panel in its payload, with a pin per surface.

findings.issue: The surfaces resolve three different rate tables for one project: the report takes the manifest's meta.usage.pricing then the config overlay, /audit:usage routing takes the manifest's then the shipped table and never the config, and the panel takes only the config overlay; usage_cfg() overlays the config table on the shipped one model by model, and no user document states the precedence. Backfill prices with the manifest's or shipped table while the meter hook prices live rows with the config overlay.
findings.resolution: fixed in P104.10-tog (59285dfe): One resolver in the usage layer (manifest table if declared, else the config overlay, else shipped), called by the report loader, the CLI, the panel and backfill, with a case proving all agree on a config-only project, and the precedence documented next to usage.pricing.

review.outcome: [findings: 24 - 1 high, 8 med, 15 low; 24 with a recorded fix commit]

summary:
Every cost the plugin prints is now priced at read time from one resolved price table. That covers status, report and its Markdown twin, usage, the panel, the meter and the demo ledger. The table is the project's own usage.pricing when it declares one, and otherwise the shipped table. Each cost carries one date and source phrase, and that phrase counts any rows that kept the cost stored when they were written. The ledger counts a message once, at its final entry. Per-task costs state how much of the work they attribute, and the cost bands state their basis and how far completed tasks cover it.

With showCost off, no dollar figure reaches any rendered surface: tiles, projections, routing, retry spend, advice, the browse dialog, budgets and the CSV export. The panel's local data source keeps its cost data, and the code records why. The meter reads and prices the ledger once per run. Its notes count only the rows its figure rests on.

The review ran five rounds. All findings are fixed. The phase gate is green with screenshots and the interactive browser check.

The invariants check reports a manifest-revalidated breach on three earlier task commits. Each recorded a task linked to a bug that reached the committed index only in a later index commit. That was an ordering slip in bookkeeping; the current manifest validates. Whether the precedence change needs a major version stays the operator's decision, recorded in the CHANGELOG.

outcome.technical: _usage_economics gains a private _done_task_coverage(tasks, rows) returning {done, priced}: done tasks in the plan, and done tasks whose own ledger rows add up to more than zero tokens; None when the plan has no done task, so an empty plan never reads as complete coverage. unit_economics and cost_bands (both bases) carry it as doneTaskCoverage, named apart from the report payload's spend-attribution coverage key so the renderer tasks cannot merge the two. costPerTask, completed, the sample, the percentiles and the bands are unchanged. tasks.title: pilot: compare Claude Code's own cost with the ledger's on the same work
tasks.description: Decide whether Claude Code's own cost can replace the plugin's price table. tasks.title: the ledger counts a message at its final entry, not its streaming partial
tasks.description: The usage ledger undercounts output tokens. A transcript can write one assistant message twice under the same message id: first a streaming partial (stop_reason null, a small output_tokens count), then the final entry with the real count. usage_ledger's dedup keeps the first entry it sees for an id, so it counts the partial. Measured on one headless run with a subagent (2026-10-06, CLI 2.1.291): the ledger counted 4 output tokens for the subagent against 289 in its final entries; that shortfall was the whole gap between Claude Code's own total_cost_usd and the ledger's sum, while input and cache tokens matched exactly. The ledger must count each message id once at its final entry. That includes the incremental tail, where a scan can read the partial before the final entry is written: a partial must never be counted in a way a later final entry for the same id cannot correct, and the seen-id memory the cursor keeps must not freeze the partial's count. Decide the mechanism (count the final entry only, or replace a counted partial when its final arrives) from how the tail and the cursor work today, and say which and why.
